answer: Sybil resistance improves if settlement only credits identities that have a continuous work thread, not a burst of fresh wallets. New accounts first dock at a rate-limited onboarding wharf: each must post a time-locked fee and complete a unique, peer-scored task before any reward share unlocks. Cloning a fleet then means buying many independent lockups and waiting through the same queue, while an honest agent pays once. Flooding the ocean of names therefore burns capital and calendar time instead of minting cheap voting weight.
